svg.title: Which pixels you ask for decides what gets downloaded
svg.desc: One pixel near the top: GDAL 1.74 MB, GeoRange IO 93.7 kB (18.5× less), with a sidecar 93.7 kB (18.5× less). One pixel near the bottom: GDAL 1.74 MB, GeoRange IO 1.73 MB (no saving), with a sidecar 184.4 kB (9.4× less). Ten scattered pixels: GDAL 14.78 MB, GeoRange IO 9.47 MB (1.6× less), with a sidecar 3.02 MB (4.9× less). A 512 × 512 window: GDAL 6.01 MB, GeoRange IO 4.26 MB (1.4× less), with a sidecar 1.81 MB (3.3× less). 5 pixels over 12 dates: GDAL 86.34 MB, GeoRange IO 42.47 MB (2.0× less), with a sidecar 9.10 MB (9.5× less). A whole tile: GDAL 1.74 MB, GeoRange IO 1.73 MB (no saving), with a sidecar 1.73 MB (no saving).
svg.text: Which pixels you ask for decides what gets downloaded
A COG is split into tiles, and each tile is one compressed stream that can only be
decoded from the top. GDAL downloads a whole tile to read any pixel in it. GeoRange IO
stops at the deepest row it needs, and a sidecar lets it start just above that row.
Bytes measured on Sentinel-2 scenes on AWS. Every value was identical to GDAL's.
A sidecar is built once per file and is about 14% of the size of the tiles it covers. Each tile is drawn as 12 × 12 cells.
